stor.environment: Vanilla Minecraft: Java Edition 1.15.2 in a single-player Creative-mode world with commands enabled. Use the English (US) language, enable subtitles, and keep Master Volume above 0%. No polar bear entity is required because the supplied /playsound command directly invokes the relevant sound event.
preconditions: The Minecraft Launcher can install and start the exact Java Edition release 1.15.2.
Use an unmodified client without mods or resource packs that replace sounds, subtitle text, or English language files.
A keyboard or equivalent input is available for opening chat and submitting the command.
The test world must permit the player to execute permission-level-2 commands; the procedure establishes this by enabling cheats.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, create or select a Java Edition installation that uses release 1.15.2, launch it, and wait for the title screen to finish loading.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft title screen is responsive and identifies the running version as 1.15.2.

steps.action: Set the client language to English (US). From the title screen, select Options..., select Language..., choose English (US), and select Done. Wait for any font or resource reload to finish.
steps.success_cue: The title-screen interface is displayed in English.

steps.action: Create a command-enabled test world. Select Singleplayer, select Create New World, set Game Mode to Creative, open More World Options..., ensure Allow Cheats is ON, and then select Create New World. The world name, seed, and world type may remain at their defaults.
steps.success_cue: The player enters a newly created world in Creative mode, and the HUD and terrain are visible.

steps.action: Do not continue until world loading is complete. Wait for nearby terrain to render, then briefly move the player using the movement controls to confirm that the game responds normally.
steps.success_cue: Nearby chunks are rendered and player movement responds without a loading pause.

steps.action: Enable the subtitle overlay. Press Esc, select Options..., select Music & Sounds..., and click Show Subtitles until its value is ON.
steps.success_cue: The Music & Sounds menu displays Show Subtitles: ON.

steps.action: In the same Music & Sounds menu, ensure the Master Volume slider is set above 0%. A clearly audible value such as 100% may be used.
steps.success_cue: The Master Volume setting is visibly greater than 0%.

steps.action: Return to active gameplay by selecting Done to leave Music & Sounds, selecting Done to leave Options if necessary, and selecting Back to Game from the pause menu.
steps.success_cue: The world view is active again and the player can move normally.

steps.action: Open the in-game chat/command entry using the Open Chat control, whose default key is T. If controls have been rebound, use the key assigned to Open Chat.
steps.success_cue: A chat input line is visible at the bottom of the screen and accepts keyboard input.

steps.action: Enter the report's command exactly as written, including the leading slash. Do not add coordinates, volume, pitch, or other optional arguments.
steps.success_cue: The complete command is visible in the chat input line with the sound identifier, master source, and @a target unchanged.

steps.action: Press Enter once to execute the command. Do not repeat the command; hand control to the observation subsystem immediately after this single execution.
steps.success_cue: The command closes the chat input without a red syntax or permission error, command feedback indicates successful sound playback, and the baby-polar-bear ambient sound event has just been emitted to the player.

stor.handoff_condition: The supplied /playsound command has just completed successfully once while English (US) and Show Subtitles: ON remain active. Begin observing the lower-right subtitle overlay immediately, without executing the command again.
uncertainties: The report does not specify a game mode, world seed, coordinates, or multiplayer requirement. A new single-player Creative world with cheats enabled is used as the minimum deterministic environment needed to run the supplied command.
The report does not explicitly specify the client language. English (US) is selected because the reported issue concerns the wording of an English subtitle.

The report does not specify audio levels or resource-pack state. Master Volume above 0% and unmodified vanilla resources are practical controls intended to ensure the supplied sound event is dispatched without customized subtitle text.
The historical menu path and /playsound command structure were externally checked for Java Edition compatibility; the exact command itself remains unchanged from the report.

stor.environment: Unmodified Minecraft Java Edition 1.8 in a local single-player Creative-mode world, using the default Minecraft resource pack and a visible HUD. No dedicated server, additional players, operator permissions, or cheats are required for the Minecraft 1.8 jukebox-based action-bar trigger.
preconditions: Install or select an official Minecraft Java Edition 1.8 launcher installation. Do not use the listed fix version or a newer version for this reproduction.
Disable client mods, shaders, and custom resource packs that could replace or alter the font or HUD renderer.
Use a Creative-mode world so a Jukebox and Music Disc can be obtained deterministically without crafting or exploration.
Keep the HUD visible so the hotbar and temporary action-bar message can be seen.
Use a normal gameplay view with enough clear ground in reach to place one Jukebox.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, select the installation configured for Java Edition 1.8 and start the game.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft 1.8 main menu is displayed, with the version identified as 1.8 on the menu screen.

steps.action: From the main menu, open Options, then Resource Packs. Ensure only the built-in Default resource pack is active; remove any custom packs from the selected list, then return to the main menu.
steps.success_cue: The game has returned to the main menu with no custom resource pack active.

steps.action: Click Singleplayer, then click Create New World.
steps.success_cue: The Create New World screen is open.

steps.action: Enter a recognizable world name, such as MC-72687, and click the Game Mode button until it reads Game Mode: Creative.
steps.success_cue: The world-creation screen shows Game Mode: Creative.

steps.action: Click Create New World and wait for generation and terrain loading to finish. Do not continue until nearby terrain is rendered and normal movement responds immediately.
steps.success_cue: The player is standing in the generated Creative world, surrounding terrain is rendered, and movement is responsive.

steps.action: Confirm that the normal gameplay HUD is visible. If the crosshair and nine-slot hotbar are hidden, press the Toggle HUD control once; its default key is F1.
steps.exact_input: F1 only if the HUD is hidden
steps.success_cue: The crosshair is visible at screen center and the nine-slot hotbar is visible along the bottom of the screen.

steps.action: Press the inventory control, default E, to open the Creative inventory.
steps.success_cue: The Creative inventory interface is open and its item-category tabs are visible.

steps.action: Select the Search Items tab, represented by a compass icon near the top of the Creative inventory.
steps.exact_input: Click the compass-icon Search Items tab
steps.success_cue: A text search field and a searchable item grid are displayed.

steps.action: Click the search field and enter jukebox.
steps.success_cue: The item grid is filtered and a Jukebox block item is visible.

steps.action: Move the Jukebox from the search results into the first hotbar slot shown along the bottom of the inventory. This can be done by clicking the Jukebox and then clicking hotbar slot 1.
steps.success_cue: A Jukebox icon is present in hotbar slot 1.

steps.action: Replace the current search text with music disc.
steps.success_cue: The item grid shows the available Music Disc items.

steps.action: Choose the Music Disc whose tooltip identifies the track as C418 - 13 and move it into hotbar slot 2.
steps.success_cue: The selected Music Disc is present in hotbar slot 2 while the Jukebox remains in slot 1.

steps.action: Press the inventory control, default E, to close the Creative inventory and return to gameplay.
steps.success_cue: The world view is visible again, with the Jukebox in hotbar slot 1 and the Music Disc in slot 2.

steps.action: Press hotbar key 1 to select the Jukebox. Aim the crosshair at the top surface of a nearby solid ground block with empty space above it.
steps.success_cue: The Jukebox is shown as the held item and the crosshair targets a valid nearby placement surface.

steps.action: Right-click the targeted ground surface once to place the Jukebox.
steps.success_cue: A Jukebox block is placed in the world within interaction reach of the player.

steps.action: Press hotbar key 2 to select the Music Disc.
steps.success_cue: The Music Disc is the active held item.

steps.action: Aim the center crosshair directly at the placed Jukebox. Keep the hotbar area unobstructed and be ready to inspect the temporary text immediately after the next action.
steps.success_cue: The Jukebox is under the crosshair and within right-click interaction range.

steps.action: Right-click the Jukebox exactly once with the Music Disc to insert and play it. Immediately hand control to the observation subsystem while the temporary 'Now playing' text is visible above the hotbar.
steps.success_cue: The disc has been accepted by the Jukebox, music playback has begun, and the temporary track-identification text is currently displayed in the action-bar area above the hotbar.

stor.handoff_condition: The Music Disc has just been inserted into the placed Jukebox in Minecraft Java Edition 1.8, and its temporary track-identification text is currently visible in the action-bar area. Begin visual inspection before that temporary message fades.
uncertainties: The report supplies the command `/title @a actionbar {"text":"MC-72687","color":"white"}`, but the required version-selection policy makes Minecraft 1.8 the recommended version. The report's own historical comments indicate that command-driven action-bar messages became available later, around the 16w32b development period, so that command is not used or modified in this Minecraft 1.8 plan.
The Minecraft 1.8 reproduction therefore uses the vanilla Jukebox track-identification message, which the supplied report comments identify as an action-bar use in vanilla Minecraft.

The report does not require a particular Music Disc. Music Disc C418 - 13 is selected only as a deterministic practical choice; another standard Minecraft 1.8 Music Disc should trigger the same type of temporary message.

If reproduction specifically through the report's exact `/title` command is required instead of through the earliest affected version, use the affected version Minecraft 16w41a in a cheats-enabled world and execute the supplied command without changing its text. That alternative is not the recommended-version procedure because Minecraft 16w41a is not the first listed affected version.

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition 1.17 Pre-release 1 in a fresh vanilla single-player world, using the English (US) language, with commands permitted. Creative mode with cheats enabled is used as the simplest deterministic environment. Do not use the fix version 22w15a or a resource pack that replaces English advancement text.
preconditions: The launcher can start the exact affected version 1.17 Pre-release 1; some launcher interfaces identify this version as 1.17-pre1.
The client language is English (US), because the report identifies English translation strings and capitalization.
No resource pack or data pack is installed that changes vanilla advancement titles or descriptions.
Use a fresh single-player world so the selected target advancement has not already been granted.
The player has permission to execute commands; the practical setup below uses Creative mode with cheats enabled.

The report permits granting any listed affected advancement. This plan selects the first listed advancement, minecraft:adventure/lightning_rod_with_villager_no_fire, as the deterministic representative case.

steps.action: Start Minecraft Java Edition using the installation configured for 1.17 Pre-release 1. At the title screen, verify the displayed version before continuing; do not continue if a different release, pre-release, release candidate, or snapshot is running.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft title screen is loaded and its version label identifies 1.17 Pre-release 1, potentially using the shorter form 1.17-pre1.

steps.action: Set the game language to English (US). From the title screen, open Options, open Language, select English (US), and confirm with Done until you return to the title screen.
steps.success_cue: The title-screen buttons and other interface text are displayed in English.

steps.action: Create a fresh single-player world. Select Creative game mode and ensure commands are permitted by setting Allow Cheats to ON, then create the world. The world name, seed, difficulty, and world type are not specified by the report and may remain at their defaults.
steps.exact_input: Singleplayer -> Create New World -> Game Mode: Creative -> Allow Cheats: ON -> Create New World
steps.success_cue: The player enters a newly created world in Creative mode, with the hotbar and crosshair visible.

steps.action: Wait for initial world loading to finish before executing the advancement command. Do not continue while the loading screen is present or while nearby terrain is still failing to render.
steps.success_cue: Nearby terrain is rendered, the player can look or move normally, and opening interfaces responds without loading delay.

steps.action: Press T to open in-game chat. Enter the report's first affected advancement command exactly as supplied, including the leading slash, and press Enter. Execute it as the local player, not from a server console, so @s selects the player whose advancement screen will be inspected.
steps.success_cue: Chat confirms that the advancement was granted to the player, and a completion notification for the advancement titled “Surge Protector” may appear.

steps.action: Open the Advancements interface by pressing the default Advancements key, L. If that control has been rebound or does not open the interface, press Esc and click Advancements from the pause menu instead.
steps.success_cue: The full-screen Advancements interface is open and at least the Adventure advancement tab is available.

steps.action: Select the Adventure tab. If the interface opened on another tab, click the tab whose root advancement is titled “Adventure.”
steps.success_cue: The Adventure advancement tree is displayed, with the completed advancement path containing “Surge Protector” available in the tree.

steps.action: Locate the completed advancement titled “Surge Protector.” It is a direct child of the Adventure root. If necessary, hold the left mouse button on an empty part of the advancement background and drag to pan the tree. Move the pointer over advancement tiles until the title “Surge Protector” is shown, then leave the pointer stationary over that tile so its title-and-description tooltip remains open. Do not evaluate or rewrite the description.
steps.exact_input: Left-click-drag to pan if needed, then mouse-hover over “Surge Protector”
steps.success_cue: The “Surge Protector” tooltip is fully visible and includes its advancement description beneath the title.

stor.handoff_condition: The English (US) Advancements interface is open on the Adventure tab, and the pointer is stationary over the completed “Surge Protector” advancement with its description tooltip fully visible. The observation subsystem should take control at this point.
uncertainties: The report does not explicitly name the client language. English (US) is selected because the reported translation keys are paired with English strings whose capitalization is under test.

The report allows any of nine affected advancements to be granted. To avoid unnecessary repetition, this plan uses the first supplied command and the corresponding “Surge Protector” advancement as a deterministic representative.

The report does not require a particular game mode, seed, coordinates, or server type. A fresh Creative single-player world with cheats enabled is a practical execution choice rather than a reported requirement.
The exact launcher-facing label may be shortened to 1.17-pre1 even though the affected-version string in the report is 1.17 Pre-release 1.
Advancement tile positions can vary with window dimensions and GUI scale, so no fixed screen coordinates are supplied; the executor must identify the tile by its “Surge Protector” title.

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition 1.21.6 in a fresh single-player world, using Survival mode with commands/cheats enabled. Use the normal in-game HUD with the locator bar enabled. A dedicated server, multiple players, specific seed, coordinates, resource pack, or non-default graphics setting is not specified by the report.
preconditions: Use exactly Minecraft Java Edition 1.21.6, the first version listed as affected.
Create a fresh world so that minecraft:recipes/brewing/blaze_powder has not already been granted to the test player.
The player must be in Survival mode. Adventure mode is also reported as affected, but Survival is used for this plan.
Enable commands/cheats when creating the world so the player can execute /gamerule, /summon, and /advancement commands.
Keep the normal HUD visible; the hotbar, hearts, and hunger bar should not be hidden by the Hide GUI control.
Do not gain or lose experience immediately before the trigger. Continue only after the locator bar has replaced the experience bar and its waypoint is steadily visible.
Do not grant the target advancement until the designated trigger step.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, select or create an installation for Java Edition 1.21.6, launch it, and verify the version shown on the title screen before continuing.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft title screen is open and identifies the running version as 1.21.6.

steps.action: Select Singleplayer, create a new world, set Game Mode to Survival, and enable commands/cheats. No particular seed or world type is required by the report; a fresh world is used to prevent the target advancement from already being granted.
steps.success_cue: The new world begins loading with the player configured for Survival mode and permitted to execute commands.

steps.action: Wait without performing advancement- or experience-granting activities until the terrain around the player has rendered and movement responds normally.
steps.success_cue: Nearby chunks are rendered, the player can move normally, and no loading screen is present.

steps.action: Confirm that the normal HUD is visible. If the hotbar, hearts, and hunger bar are hidden, press the bound Hide GUI control once; its default key is F1. Do not press F1 if the HUD is already visible.
steps.success_cue: The hotbar is visible at the bottom of the screen, with the Survival health and hunger indicators visible above it.

steps.action: Press T, the default Open Chat control, to open the in-game chat and command input.
steps.success_cue: A text input line is open at the bottom of the screen and accepts keyboard input.

steps.action: Enter the command exactly as shown, including the leading slash, to ensure that the locator bar game rule is enabled. Do not submit it until the complete command has been entered.
steps.success_cue: The unsent chat input reads exactly: /gamerule locatorBar true

steps.action: Press Enter to execute the locator-bar game-rule command. The locatorBar game rule is available in Java Edition 1.21.6 and enables waypoint display. ([minecraft.net](https://www.minecraft.net/de-de/article/minecraft-java-edition-1-21-6?utm_source=openai))
steps.success_cue: The command is accepted without a syntax or permission error, and command feedback indicates that locatorBar is true.

steps.action: Press T again to open the in-game chat and command input.
steps.success_cue: The chat input line is open and ready for another command.

steps.action: Enter the report's armor-stand summon command exactly as written, including the leading slash, lowercase identifiers, braces, quotation marks, attribute ID, and base value. Do not submit it until the entire command is present.
steps.success_cue: The unsent chat input exactly matches the supplied armor-stand summon command.

steps.action: Press Enter to execute the summon command at the player's current coordinates.
steps.success_cue: The command succeeds without a syntax error, and an armor stand exists at or immediately beside the position where the player executed the command.

steps.action: Walk approximately 10 to 20 blocks horizontally away from the armor stand, remaining well inside its configured 100-block transmission range. Turn the camera back toward the armor stand; keeping the armor stand itself in view is the simplest way to ensure the camera faces its waypoint.
steps.exact_input: Use the movement controls, normally W/A/S/D, and mouse movement to face the armor stand.
steps.success_cue: The player is 10 to 20 blocks from the armor stand, the armor stand's chunk remains loaded, and the camera is facing toward it.

steps.action: Stop moving and wait until the locator bar is displayed in the HUD area normally occupied by the experience bar. Keep facing the armor stand and do not collect experience, use an anvil or enchanting table, or execute an advancement command during this wait. Entities with waypoint_transmit_range above zero can transmit waypoints to players within range. ([minecraft.wiki](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Player_Locator_Bar?utm_source=openai))
steps.success_cue: A colored waypoint indicator for the armor stand is steadily visible on the locator bar, and the normal experience bar is not currently occupying that HUD area.

steps.action: Without changing position or turning away from the armor stand, press T to open chat while preserving the visible-waypoint setup.
steps.success_cue: The command input is open, and the player remains within 100 blocks of and oriented toward the armor stand.

steps.action: Enter the report's first advancement command exactly as shown, including the leading slash. Do not press Enter yet.
steps.success_cue: The complete unsent command /advancement grant @s only minecraft:recipes/brewing/blaze_powder is visible in the chat input.

steps.action: Press Enter once to submit the advancement grant command. This is the trigger action; do not grant additional advancements or perform another action before handing off to HUD observation.
steps.success_cue: The command has been submitted without a syntax or permission error, and command feedback confirms that the specified advancement was granted to the current player.

stor.handoff_condition: The armor stand's waypoint was steadily visible immediately before the player submitted /advancement grant @s only minecraft:recipes/brewing/blaze_powder, and that command has just been executed. Hand off immediately for observation of the HUD beginning at the Enter keypress; do not execute the report's alternative plant_seed command unless a separate clean trial is requested.
uncertainties: The report does not specify whether the test was performed in single-player, on an integrated multiplayer world, or on a dedicated server. This plan uses a fresh single-player world because the supplied commands and waypoint-transmitting armor stand allow the stated setup without another player.
The report does not provide a world seed, coordinates, or world type. None are introduced as requirements.

The phrase "Viewing Waypoints" does not specify the player's distance or camera orientation. The plan uses a 10-to-20-block separation and faces the armor stand so its waypoint can be visibly confirmed while remaining inside the supplied 100-block transmission range.

The report supplies both minecraft:recipes/brewing/blaze_powder and minecraft:husbandry/plant_seed as examples. The plan uses only the first command so one advancement grant provides a single, clean trigger.
The report does not state whether the target recipe advancement had previously been granted. A fresh world is used to avoid that ambiguity rather than adding an unreported advancement-revoke command.
The exact armor-stand summon and advancement commands are preserved from the report and are not modernized or replaced.

preconditions: Configure the Minecraft Launcher so that Minecraft Java Edition snapshot 22w03a can be launched.
Use a disposable new world; the reproduction requires leaving and reopening the same save.
Be prepared to pause and leave the world immediately after teleporting, before the falling player descends to Y=320.
If controls have been rebound, use the bindings for Open Chat and Game Menu instead of the default T and Esc keys.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, select the installation/profile that runs Java Edition snapshot 22w03a, and launch the game.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft main menu is visible and identifies the running version as 22w03a.

steps.action: From the main menu, open the single-player world list and start creating a new world by selecting Singleplayer and then Create New World.
steps.success_cue: The Create New World configuration screen is open.

steps.action: Set Allow Cheats to ON. The report does not specify a seed, difficulty, or game mode, so leave those settings at their existing defaults.
steps.success_cue: The world-creation screen visibly shows that cheats are enabled.

steps.action: Select Create New World and wait for world generation and initial loading to finish.

steps.action: Before continuing, wait until nearby terrain has rendered and normal player input responds. Do not leave and reopen the world yet.

steps.action: Initiate reloading of the selected world by clicking Play Selected World or by double-clicking the selected world entry.
steps.success_cue: The world-loading sequence begins and the Loading terrain... screen is displayed.

steps.action: Leave the loading attempt uninterrupted for approximately thirty seconds. Do not press Esc, close the client, switch worlds, or provide movement input during this interval.
steps.success_cue: Approximately thirty seconds have elapsed since the same saved world began reloading, with no user action interrupting the attempt.

stor.handoff_condition: The same world has been reopened after the player was saved above Y=320, and the resulting loading attempt has been left uninterrupted for approximately thirty seconds. The observation subsystem should now evaluate the client's current state.
uncertainties: The report does not specify a game mode, difficulty, or world seed. This plan leaves those settings at their world-creation defaults and changes only Allow Cheats to ON.

The report states that the issue can occur above Y=320 or below Y=-64 and in any dimension. This plan uses the report's primary and simplest deterministic variant: teleporting to Y=1000 in the newly created Overworld.

The report gives no exact maximum delay between teleporting and leaving the world. The player must open the Game Menu promptly after teleportation so that the save is closed before the player falls to Y=320 or lower.

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition, Minecraft 1.12 Pre-Release 3, vanilla single-player world using the integrated server, Creative mode, and cheats enabled. Use a disposable test world with an open placement area. No seed, dedicated server, additional player, mod, resource pack, or datapack is required by the report.
preconditions: Configure the Minecraft Launcher to run exactly Minecraft 1.12 Pre-Release 3, the first version listed as affected. Do not use fix version 25w02a.
Use a new or disposable Creative-mode world with cheats enabled so that command blocks can be obtained and commands requiring permission level 2 can be run.
Use the default interaction controls or their rebound equivalents: T opens chat, E opens inventory, Esc closes a UI, and right-click places, opens, or operates the targeted block.
Choose a location where a command block can be placed with air directly above it and with at least one exposed side available for a lever.
Do not place any block in the air space directly above the command block before the first activation.
Preserve the exact legacy command from the report comment. The main description was later rewritten using 1.13 command syntax, which is not appropriate for the recommended 1.12 pre-release.

steps.action: Launch the installation configured for Minecraft 1.12 Pre-Release 3 and wait at the title screen until startup has completed.
steps.success_cue: The game reaches its title screen and identifies the running client as the selected 1.12 pre-release rather than a later release or snapshot.

steps.action: Select Singleplayer, choose Create New World, set Game Mode to Creative, open More World Options, ensure Allow Cheats is ON, and create the world. Wait until terrain has rendered and player movement responds normally.
steps.exact_input: Singleplayer -> Create New World -> Game Mode: Creative -> More World Options -> Allow Cheats: ON -> Create New World
steps.success_cue: A Creative-mode world is loaded, surrounding terrain is visible, and the player can move and open chat.

steps.action: Move to a level, accessible location. If necessary, left-click blocks in Creative mode to clear a placement space. Reserve one ground-level position for a command block, keep the block space directly above it as air, and keep at least one side exposed for a lever.
steps.success_cue: There is a clear command-block position with air immediately above it and an accessible side face.

steps.action: Press T to open in-game chat, enter the command including the leading slash, and press Enter to obtain one command block.
steps.success_cue: A command block item is present in the player's inventory or hotbar.

steps.action: Press T again, enter the command including the leading slash, and press Enter to obtain one lever for controlled repeated activation.
steps.success_cue: A lever item is present in the player's inventory or hotbar.

steps.action: Press E to open the inventory. Ensure the command block and lever are each in a hotbar slot—the nine slots along the bottom of the inventory. If either item is elsewhere, click it and then click an empty hotbar slot to move it there. Close the inventory with E or Esc.
steps.success_cue: Both the command block and lever are visible in separate hotbar slots and can be selected with the corresponding number keys or mouse wheel.

steps.action: Select the command block in the hotbar. Aim at the prepared ground position and right-click to place it. Do not place anything in the air block directly above it.
steps.success_cue: One command block is placed, its top face has air immediately above it, and one side remains accessible.

steps.action: Right-click the placed command block to open its configuration screen. In the command text field, enter the exact report command without a leading slash. Leave it as an impulse command block that is unconditional and needs redstone, then select Done.
steps.success_cue: The command block configuration closes, and the command block is ready to place a dropper exactly one block above itself when powered.

steps.action: Select the lever in the hotbar, aim at an exposed side face of the command block, and right-click to attach the lever. Do not operate it yet.
steps.success_cue: A lever is attached to the command block and is visibly in its initial off position; the space above the command block is still air.

steps.action: Right-click the lever once to change it from off to on and provide the command block's first redstone activation. Wait until the block update is visible.
steps.success_cue: A dropper is visible directly above the command block, confirming that the first command execution placed its target block.

steps.action: Aim at the dropper above the command block and right-click it to open the dropper inventory. Inspect the 3-by-3 container grid only to confirm that the first execution established the required starting inventory.
steps.success_cue: The dropper interface is open and contains one stone block in its container grid; do not move or remove the stone.

steps.action: Press Esc to close the dropper interface without clicking or moving any inventory item.
steps.success_cue: The world view is restored, the dropper remains directly above the command block, and its stone has not been manually altered.

steps.action: Right-click the attached lever once to return it from on to off. Do not break or replace either block.
steps.success_cue: The lever is visibly off, the command block is no longer powered, and the existing dropper remains above it ready for the second execution.

steps.action: Right-click the lever once more to change it from off to on. This issues the exact same setblock command a second time against the already-existing dropper. Do not open, break, or otherwise alter the dropper after this activation before handing off.
steps.success_cue: The lever has just completed a second off-to-on transition, the command block has received its second activation, and the target dropper remains in place for immediate inspection.

stor.handoff_condition: The exact report command has just been executed for the second time against the existing dropper, and the dropper remains one block above the command block. Hand control to the Observation Agent now, before any further player interaction, so it can inspect command execution status and the dropper's retained block-entity data and inventory state.
uncertainties: The report's main Description examples use syntax updated to the 1.13 command format, while the required recommended version is Minecraft 1.12 Pre-Release 3. This plan therefore uses the exact legacy command supplied in Comment 1, which was written for the original 1.12-era reproduction and reproduces the same repeated-/setblock inventory condition.

The report does not require a particular game mode, world seed, coordinate, dedicated server, or multiplayer setup. A disposable single-player Creative world with cheats is used as the simplest deterministic execution environment.

The report comment specifically says to put the command in a command block and run it twice. The command block and lever arrangement is an operational implementation of that instruction; the lever itself is not asserted to be a bug requirement.
This plan exercises the /setblock variant only. The report also states that /fill is affected, but reproducing both command variants is unnecessary to reach the documented trigger.

The report's legacy command omits an explicit Slot tag in the Items entry. It is preserved exactly because the reporter states that the first execution places a stone in the dropper; the plan requires confirming that starting state before triggering the second execution.

stor.environment: Minecraft: Java Edition snapshot 17w48a in a new single-player Creative-mode Superflat world using the integrated server. Cheats must be enabled, command feedback and visible chat must be available, and no mods, plugins, custom data packs, or additional players should be present.
preconditions: Configure the launcher to start the exact affected snapshot Minecraft 17w48a, not a later 1.13 snapshot, release, or the listed fix version.
Use a fresh world so no entity already has the scoreboard tag named `test`.
Use English (US) if the observation subsystem will compare the command feedback text to the wording in the report.
Enable cheats so the player can execute permission-level-2 commands from in-game chat.

The plan creates six stationary armor stands at distinct distances and removes unrelated entities so both selectors resolve to the same nearest five entities, with exactly one additional entity selected by the second command.
After choosing the test position, do not walk, fly, teleport, place entities, drop items, or otherwise change entity distances until both reported `/tag` commands have completed.

steps.action: Launch Minecraft: Java Edition using the exact installation/profile for snapshot 17w48a. Confirm the version text on the title screen before continuing.
steps.success_cue: The title screen identifies the running game as Minecraft 17w48a.

steps.action: Set the client language to English (US): from the title screen open Options, open Language, select English (US), and confirm with Done.
steps.success_cue: Title-screen and menu text is displayed in English.

steps.action: Create a fresh test world. Select Singleplayer, Create New World, choose Creative mode, open More World Options, set Allow Cheats to ON, select the Superflat world type, disable structure generation if that option is shown, and create the world. No particular seed is required.
steps.success_cue: A new Creative-mode Superflat world is open and the player can fly and use commands.

steps.action: Ensure chat messages are visible. Press Esc, open Options, open Chat Settings, set Chat to Shown, and return to the world.
steps.success_cue: The Chat setting is Shown and the player has returned to gameplay.

steps.action: Wait until the surrounding flat terrain has rendered and movement responds normally. Stand still on an open, level part of the Superflat surface with at least 14 unobstructed blocks available in the positive X direction. Release all movement controls and retain this position for the remainder of the reproduction.
steps.success_cue: Terrain is loaded, the player is stationary on level ground, and a straight open area extends at least 14 blocks in one world-axis direction.

steps.action: Enable command feedback explicitly. Press T to open in-game chat, enter the command including its leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: The gamerule command completes and subsequent command responses can appear in chat.

steps.action: Prevent new natural mobs from entering the selector during the test. Press T, enter the command including the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: Natural mob spawning is disabled for the test world.

steps.action: Remove all existing non-player entities before creating the controlled targets. Press T, enter the command including the leading slash, and press Enter. Wait about one second and execute the same command again to remove any drops or experience orbs created by the first pass. Repeat until an execution reports that no matching entity was found. Do not move the player while doing this.
steps.success_cue: A final cleanup attempt finds no non-player entity; only the stationary player remains as an entity in the immediate test area.

steps.action: Create the first stationary target two blocks away along positive X. Without moving, press T, enter the command including its leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: One armor stand is visible on the ground two blocks in the positive X direction from the stationary player.

steps.action: Create the second stationary target four blocks away along positive X. Without moving, press T, enter the command including its leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: A second armor stand is visible farther along the same line, with two armor stands now present at distinct distances.

steps.action: Create the third stationary target six blocks away along positive X. Without moving, press T, enter the command including its leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: A third armor stand is visible on the same line, distinct from the first two.

steps.action: Create the fourth stationary target eight blocks away along positive X. Without moving, press T, enter the command including its leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: A fourth armor stand is visible on the same line at a greater distance.

steps.action: Create the fifth stationary target ten blocks away along positive X. Without moving, press T, enter the command including its leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: A fifth armor stand is visible on the same line at a distinct distance.

steps.action: Create the sixth stationary target twelve blocks away along positive X. Without moving, press T, enter the command including its leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: Six armor stands are present in one line at distinct distances of approximately 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, and 12 blocks from the stationary player, with no unrelated entities nearby.

steps.action: Establish the partial preexisting-tag condition using the report's first command. Do not move or alter any entities. Press T, enter the command exactly as written including its leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: The first command executes successfully, and the five entities selected as nearest now have the `test` tag.

steps.action: Immediately execute the report's second command without moving the player or changing any entity. Press T, enter the command exactly as written including its leading slash, and press Enter. After it completes, issue no further commands and leave the newest feedback line visible for the observation subsystem.
steps.success_cue: The second `/tag` command has completed while the player and all controlled entities remained in the same positions, and its feedback line is available in chat for inspection.

stor.handoff_condition: The second command, `/tag @e[sort=nearest,limit=6] add test`, has just completed with the same entity arrangement used by the first command. The latest command feedback remains visible in chat; hand control to the observation subsystem now.
uncertainties: The report does not specify a game mode, world type, seed, coordinates, or method for supplying nearby entities. Creative mode, a Superflat world, cleanup commands, and six armor stands are deterministic implementation choices rather than report requirements.
The helper commands used to suppress, remove, and summon entities are not part of the report's original reproduction commands. The two `/tag` commands are preserved exactly as supplied.

The controlled setup deliberately provides at least six entities at distinct distances regardless of whether the executing player is included among the nearest selector results. This avoids relying on tied distances or random natural mob placement.

If the exact historical client rejects an optional helper command despite the version verification, the equivalent fallback is to disable or remove unrelated entities manually and place six armor stands at distinct distances without moving between the two reported `/tag` commands; the reported commands themselves must not be changed.

stor.environment: Unmodified Minecraft Java Edition 1.21 client using a new, expendable singleplayer Creative-mode world with commands enabled. Execute every supplied command through in-game chat, including the leading slash. Keep the active game directory's logs/latest.log available to the separate observation subsystem.
preconditions: Launch the exact affected Java Edition version 1.21, not the fixed version 25w07a or a later version.
Use an expendable world because the procedure places NBT-bearing blocks, summons falling-block entities, and modifies a monster spawner.
Create or load the world in Creative mode with Allow Cheats enabled so that /give, /summon, and /data can be executed.
Use an unmodified client without mods or datapacks that alter commands, block entities, falling blocks, spawners, or logging.
Ensure there is a loaded, level area with a solid floor and enough open space to place suspicious sand and a monster spawner.
Ensure the inventory has room for suspicious sand, a breeze spawn egg, and a monster spawner.
Identify the game instance's current logs/latest.log before triggering the cases so the observation subsystem can inspect the correct live log.
Do not place the invalid-Name summon command in a repeating command block; a single execution is sufficient before the final deterministic spawner trigger.

steps.action: Start Minecraft Java Edition using the 1.21 installation profile, then select Singleplayer.
steps.success_cue: The main menu identifies the running version as Minecraft Java Edition 1.21, and the singleplayer world list is open.

steps.action: Create a new expendable world. Set Game Mode to Creative and set Allow Cheats to ON, then create the world. If an existing expendable Creative world with commands enabled is used instead, load that world.
steps.success_cue: The player is in a Creative-mode world where commands can be executed.

steps.action: Wait before continuing until nearby terrain is fully rendered and movement responds normally.
steps.success_cue: Surrounding chunks are visible, the player can move without initial loading pauses, and chat can be opened.

steps.action: Move to a level, solid area with several empty blocks of space. Use separate nearby positions for the suspicious-sand block and the later monster spawner so they do not overlap.
steps.success_cue: A solid floor and unobstructed placement locations are available within reach.

steps.action: Locate the active game directory's logs/latest.log outside the game and make its path available to the observation subsystem. Leave Minecraft running and do not evaluate the log contents during these setup steps.
steps.success_cue: The observation subsystem can access the live latest.log belonging to the running 1.21 instance.

steps.action: Press T to open in-game chat. Enter the report's suspicious-sand command exactly as written, including the leading slash, and press Enter once.
steps.success_cue: A suspicious-sand item has been added to the player's inventory; the command is not executed a second time.

steps.action: If the suspicious sand is not already in the hotbar, press E to open the inventory, locate the suspicious-sand item, and move it into any hotbar slot. Close the inventory with E or Esc, then select that slot using its number key or the mouse wheel.
steps.success_cue: Suspicious sand is visible in the player's hand and its hotbar slot is highlighted.

steps.action: Aim at the top face of an empty solid floor block and use the selected suspicious sand once with right-click, or the bound Use Item/Place Block control, to place it.

steps.action: Move a few blocks away from the placed suspicious sand so the next falling-block summons have unobstructed space at the player's current coordinates.
steps.success_cue: The player is standing in an open location and is not inside the placed suspicious-sand block.

steps.action: Press T to open chat. Enter the report's falling-block command with the invalid BlockState Name exactly as written, including the leading slash, and press Enter once. Do not use a repeating command block.
steps.success_cue: The command has been submitted exactly once and control has returned to the player; no persistent summoned entity is required as a progress check.

steps.action: Wait only until the command submission has finished processing and player movement responds again. Do not repeatedly execute the command even if no falling block remains visible.
steps.success_cue: Player controls respond normally enough to submit the next command.

steps.action: Press T to open chat. Enter the report's falling-block command with the invalid LootTable exactly as written, including the leading slash, and press Enter once.
steps.success_cue: The command has been submitted exactly once and control has returned to the player; the test does not depend on the falling block remaining visible.

steps.action: Prepare the report's spawn egg for the spawner case. Press T, enter the exact /give command including the leading slash, and press Enter once.
steps.success_cue: A breeze spawn egg containing the supplied entity data has been added to the inventory.

steps.action: Press E if necessary, move the command-provided breeze spawn egg into a hotbar slot, close the inventory, and select that hotbar slot.
steps.success_cue: The command-provided breeze spawn egg is visible in the player's hand and its hotbar slot is highlighted.

stor.environment: Minecraft: Java Edition client snapshot 23w07a, using the single-player Create New World interface. Launch Minecraft: Java Edition 23w07a and wait until the main title menu is fully visible and responsive.
Use the normal single-player new-world workflow. No existing world is needed.
Do not click the final "Create New World" button at any point; the trigger occurs while configuring the uncreated world.

When the Experiments screen is opened for the first time, both experimental-feature toggles must begin in their disabled state. If either is already enabled, cancel out of world creation and start a fresh Create New World configuration before continuing.
Use left-click for button and toggle activation unless the client is being operated through keyboard UI navigation.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, select the installation configured for snapshot 23w07a and launch it. Wait through loading and any first-launch screens until the Minecraft main title menu is responsive.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft title menu is visible, and the running game version is 23w07a.

steps.action: On the title menu, left-click "Singleplayer".
steps.success_cue: The Select World screen is open. It does not matter whether existing worlds are listed.

steps.action: On the Select World screen, left-click "Create New World". This opens configuration for a new world but does not create it yet.

steps.success_cue: The Experiments screen is open and displays exactly two experimental-feature toggle rows.

steps.action: Inspect both experiment toggles and confirm that each is currently disabled. If a toggle is already enabled, stop this attempt and restart from a fresh Create New World configuration rather than toggling it off here.
steps.success_cue: Both experiment toggles are visibly in their disabled state before either is changed.

steps.action: Left-click the first experiment toggle once so that it changes from disabled to enabled. Do not click it again.
steps.success_cue: The first experiment toggle is visibly enabled, while the second remains disabled.

steps.action: Left-click the second experiment toggle once so that it also changes from disabled to enabled.
steps.success_cue: Both experiment toggles are visibly enabled at the same time.

steps.action: Left-click "Done" at the bottom of the Experiments screen to save the enabled experiment selections and return toward the Create New World screen. Do not click the final Create New World button.
steps.success_cue: The enabled selections have been submitted, and the client either returns to Create New World or presents an experimental-feature confirmation dialog.

steps.action: If a warning or confirmation dialog about using experimental features appears, choose the affirmative option that proceeds with the enabled experiments. If no such dialog appears, perform no extra action. Wait until the Create New World configuration screen is responsive again.
steps.success_cue: The client is back on the Create New World configuration screen, and no world has been created.

steps.success_cue: The second Done activation has just been issued after both experiment toggles were changed through the sequence disabled to enabled to disabled, with no subsequent UI input.

stor.handoff_condition: Both experimental-feature toggles were enabled, saved with Done, reopened, disabled, and the second Done button has just been activated. No world has been created and no subsequent dialog button has been pressed. Begin observing the client UI, world-creation state, and client log.

The report does not state the displayed names of the two experiment toggles. The plan therefore identifies them by their two visible rows and preserves the instruction to operate both, rather than assigning potentially incorrect labels.

The report does not specify whether 23w07a presents an experimental-feature warning after the first Done activation. A conditional confirmation step is included so the executor can return to Create New World without creating the world.

steps.action: After bugreport:test/1 completes, wait at least one second before entering the next command. This ensures the separate control invocation is not being executed in the same game tick as the actual trigger invocation.
steps.success_cue: At least one second has elapsed, gameplay remains responsive, and the player is still in the Overworld.

steps.action: Open in-game chat again using the Open Chat control, default T.
steps.success_cue: The chat input field is visible and ready for the trigger command.

steps.action: Run the report's second function by entering the command exactly as shown, including the leading slash, and pressing Enter. Do not insert any additional command between its internal operations: this function sets the bugreport:test timeline to 0, reads and prints the environment attribute, and then invokes bugreport:test/1 within the same function execution.
steps.success_cue: The command is accepted without an unknown-function or permission error and bugreport:test/2 completes, producing its chat output.

uncertainties: The raw report does not expose the attachment's internal archive structure. The plan assumes "Bugreport Datapack.zip" is directly importable. The report does not explicitly state whether the first function invocation must be separated from the second by a particular delay. Waiting at least one second is a practical safeguard ensuring that the two manually issued commands occur in different ticks; the same-tick accesses relevant to the trigger remain internal to bugreport:test/2.
Exact printed cloud-height values are deliberately not used as setup success criteria because evaluating those values belongs to the observation subsystem.

Web verification was limited to confirming availability/launch guidance for 26.1 Pre-Release 1 and the normal Java Edition datapack installation and verification procedure; the supplied Mojira report remains the source of truth for the function order and identifiers.

Use a keyboard whose Backspace key is known to work outside the anvil name field.
Create or open a world in which the player can obtain and place an anvil. A new Creative-mode single-player world is the selected practical setup.
Use default controls unless they have been rebound: E opens the inventory, T opens chat, number keys select hotbar slots, right-click uses or places a block, and Esc closes the current screen.
Have one ordinary renameable item available. Because the report does not specify the item, this plan uses a Stick as a simple deterministic test item.

steps.success_cue: The Minecraft main menu is open and identifies the running version as 1.20.3 Pre-Release 1.

steps.exact_input: Singleplayer -> Create New World -> Game Mode: Creative -> Create New World
steps.success_cue: The player has spawned in a Creative-mode world.

steps.success_cue: Nearby terrain is visible and the player can look and move normally.

steps.action: Perform a control check for the physical Backspace key. Press T, or the rebound Open Chat control, to focus the chat input field.
steps.success_cue: The chat interface is open and its text-entry field is focused.

steps.action: Type the control text into the chat input field. Do not press Enter or send the message.
steps.success_cue: The unsent chat input visibly reads ABC.

steps.action: Press Backspace once while the chat input field remains focused.

steps.action: Press Esc to close chat without sending the control text.
steps.success_cue: The chat interface is closed and normal world controls are active.

steps.success_cue: The anvil interface is open, showing two input slots on the left, an arrow, and an output slot on the right.

steps.action: In the player inventory or hotbar area at the bottom of the anvil interface, left-click the Stick to pick it up with the cursor. Then left-click the first anvil input slot—the leftmost slot before the plus sign—to place the Stick into it.

steps.action: Left-click inside the item-name text field near the right edge of its displayed text so the insertion caret is positioned after the existing item name.

preconditions: Install or create a Minecraft Launcher installation that uses the exact Java Edition snapshot 24w36a.

Use a mouse whose wheel generates discrete scrolling input in Minecraft.
Use default vanilla bundle behavior; do not install datapacks or mods that alter inventories, item tooltips, bundles, or mouse-wheel input.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, select the installation configured for snapshot 24w36a and start the game. Confirm the version shown on the title screen before proceeding.

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition client running 1.21.9 Release Candidate 1. Use the Singleplayer variant of the report so that no external server is required. Use a mouse or automated pointer input capable of issuing the second click reliably less than 250 milliseconds after the first click. steps.action: Identify and record a screen coordinate inside the “MC-302362 timing test” world row that is not on the row’s play button. Use the world-name text or another empty portion of the row rather than the triangular play control displayed on the world icon. Do not double-click the row.
steps.success_cue: A reusable pointer coordinate inside the named world row has been recorded, and that coordinate is outside the play button.

steps.success_cue: The first click has been issued and the client has begun switching from the main menu to the Select World screen.

The report specifies an interval within 250 milliseconds but does not define whether it was measured between mouse-button presses, releases, or processed click events. Scheduling the second press approximately 150 milliseconds after the first press is a practical choice intended to remain clearly inside the stated limit.
The exact screen coordinate of the safe world-row click depends on window geometry and GUI scale. It must therefore be calibrated in the same unchanged window before the timing-critical attempt.
The report states that the second click may be anywhere on the world or server except its play button. This plan uses the world-name area as a practical, visually identifiable non-play-button target.
